text: The report identifies 15 named gene families as essential in all 48 organisms, with no exceptions.
quote: The absolute core of bacterial life: ribosomal proteins (rpsC, rplW, rplK, rplB, rplA, rplF, rps11, rpsJ, rpsI, rpsM), chaperonin (groEL), CTP synthase (pyrG), translation elongation factor G (fusA), valyl-tRNA synthetase (valS), and geranyltranstransferase (SelGGPS). These 15 families span all 48 organisms with no exceptions.
heading: 15 Gene Families Are Essential in All 48 Bacteria

text: Among 17,222 ortholog families across 48 bacteria, the report classifies 859 (5.0%) as universally essential, 4,799 (27.9%) as variably essential, and 11,564 (67.1%) as never essential; 839 of the universally essential families meet its strict single-copy criterion and 20 contain paralogs.
quote: Of 17,222 ortholog families across 48 bacteria, 859 (5.0%) are universally essential. Of these, 839 are strict single-copy families (copy ratio <=1.5, no non-essential paralogs); 20 contain paralogs. 4,799 families (27.9%) are variably essential -- essential in some organisms, non-essential in others. 11,564 (67.1%) are never essential.
heading: Only 5% of Ortholog Families Are Universally Essential

text: The report identifies 7,084 orphan essential genes, of which 58.7% are hypothetical, versus 8.2% of universally essential genes.
quote: 7,084 essential genes have no orthologs in any other FB organism. These are 58.7% hypothetical -- the least characterized yet most functionally important genes in each organism. By contrast, universally essential genes are only 8.2% hypothetical.
heading: Orphan Essential Genes Are 58.7% Hypothetical

text: Module transfer produced 1,382 family-backed function predictions for hypothetical essential genes, covering 35.3% of predictable targets; leading predicted functions were TIGR00254, PF00460, and PF00356.
quote: Module transfer via non-essential orthologs in ICA fitness modules generated 1,382 function predictions for hypothetical essential genes (35.3% of predictable targets). All predictions are family-backed. Top predicted functions: TIGR00254 (signal transduction), PF00460 (flagellar basal body rod), PF00356 (lactoylglutathione lyase).
heading: 1,382 Function Predictions for Hypothetical Essentials

text: The key-findings section reports 91.7% core status for universally essential genes, 80.7% for non-essential genes, and 49.5% for orphan essentials; 71% of universally essential families are completely core within their species.
quote: Universally essential genes are 91.7% core vs 80.7% for non-essential. 71% of universally essential families are 100% core across all genomes in their species. Orphan essentials are only 49.5% core -- strain-specific essential functions.
heading: Universally Essential Families Are Overwhelmingly Core

text: The analysis covers 221,005 genes in 48 organisms, with 41,059 classified as essential (18.6%).
quote: - **221,005 genes** across 48 organisms, **41,059 essential** (18.6%)
heading: Essential Gene Landscape

text: Organism-level essentiality rates range from 12.2% in Pedo557 to 29.7% in Magneto.
quote: - Essentiality rate ranges from 12.2% (*Pedo557*) to 29.7% (*Magneto*)
heading: Essential Gene Landscape

text: The orthology analysis used 2,838,750 bidirectional-best-hit pairs to derive 17,222 ortholog groups across the 48 organisms.
quote: - **2,838,750 BBH pairs** yield **17,222 ortholog groups** spanning all 48 organisms
heading: Essential Gene Landscape

text: Essential genes have a median length of 675 bp versus 885 bp for non-essential genes; 17.8% of essential genes are under 300 bp.
quote: - Essential genes are shorter than non-essential (median 675 bp vs 885 bp); 17.8% of essentials are <300 bp
heading: Essential Gene Landscape

text: The family-classification table defines “universally essential” as essential in every organism where the family has members, not necessarily present in all 48 organisms.
quote: | Universally essential | 859 | 5.0% | Essential in every organism where family has members |
heading: Family Classification

text: Variably essential families have median essentiality penetrance of 33%; 813 families exceed 50% and 704 fall below 10%.
quote: Variably essential families have median essentiality penetrance of 33%. 813 families are >50% essential, 704 are <10% essential.
heading: Family Classification

text: The conservation hierarchy table assigns 6,963 genes to the universally essential class and reports 91.7% core status.
quote: | Universally essential | 91.7% | 6,963 |
heading: Conservation Hierarchy

text: The conservation hierarchy table reports 90,844 genes and 88.9% core status for the variably essential class.
quote: | Variably essential | 88.9% | 90,844 |
heading: Conservation Hierarchy

text: The conservation hierarchy table reports 47,140 genes and 81.7% core status for the never-essential class; this is a differently labeled denominator from the key-findings section’s 80.7% figure for “non-essential.”
quote: | Never essential | 81.7% | 47,140 |
heading: Conservation Hierarchy

text: The conservation hierarchy table includes 4,683 orphan essential genes with 49.5% core status; it does not explain how this subset relates to the report’s 7,084 total orphan essentials.
quote: | Orphan essential | 49.5% | 4,683 |
heading: Conservation Hierarchy

text: Essentiality penetrance has a weak positive association with core fraction (rho=0.123, p=1.6e-17), while clade size does not predict essentiality rate (rho=-0.13, p=0.36).
quote: Weak positive correlation between essentiality penetrance and core fraction (rho=0.123, p=1.6e-17): families essential in more organisms tend to be slightly more core (97.1% for >80% penetrance vs 92.8% for <20%). Clade size does NOT predict essentiality rate (rho=-0.13, p=0.36).
heading: Conservation Hierarchy

text: There are 8,297 hypothetical essential genes across 48 organisms, comprising 20.2% of all essential genes.
quote: - 8,297 hypothetical essential genes across 48 organisms (20.2% of all essentials)
heading: Function Predictions

text: Of the hypothetical essential genes, 3,912 have orthologs and are predictable by this method, while 4,385 are orphan genes that the method cannot predict.
quote: - 3,912 have orthologs (predictable); 4,385 are orphans (not predictable by this method)
heading: Function Predictions

text: Predictions span all 48 organisms, ranging from 90 for pseudo1_N1B4 to 1 for Caulo.
quote: - Predictions span 48 organisms, from 90 predictions (pseudo1_N1B4) to 1 (Caulo)
heading: Function Predictions

text: The report distinguishes its experimentally defined essential set from computationally conserved gene sets by requiring lethal transposon disruption across the tested organisms.
quote: Our experimentally-defined universally essential set is smaller because it is restricted to genes where transposon disruption is lethal across all 48 tested organisms, which is more stringent than computational conservation.
heading: The Essential Genome Is Small and Deeply Conserved

text: The report interprets variable essentiality as widespread across its 48-organism panel and relates it to prior within-species work on Streptococcus pneumoniae; it describes the panel as spanning Proteobacteria, Bacteroidetes, Firmicutes, and Archaea.
quote: The largest category is variably essential families (4,799, 28%) -- genes essential in some organisms but dispensable in others. With a median essentiality penetrance of 33%, most essential gene families are essential in only a minority of organisms. This directly extends Rosconi et al. (2022), who demonstrated within *S. pneumoniae* that the pan-genome makes gene essentiality "strain-dependent and evolvable." Our analysis shows this principle holds across 48 phylogenetically diverse species spanning Proteobacteria, Bacteroidetes, Firmicutes, and Archaea.
heading: Variable Essentiality Is the Norm, Not the Exception

text: The report proposes paralogs, alternative pathways, and accessory-genome compensation as explanations for variable essentiality; its broad-spectrum antibiotic-target inference is an interpretation rather than a tested drug-efficacy result.
quote: Variable essentiality implies that whether a gene is essential depends on genomic context -- the presence of paralogs, alternative pathways, or compensatory functions in the accessory genome. This has implications for antibiotic target selection: only the 859 universally essential families are reliable broad-spectrum targets.
heading: Variable Essentiality Is the Norm, Not the Exception

text: Recently acquired genes, rapid evolution, and lineage-specific innovation are proposed—not established—explanations for orphan essentials; the report compares them with 149 of 473 genes (31%) of unknown function in a minimal Mycoplasma genome.
quote: They represent strain-specific essential functions that may include recently acquired genes, rapidly evolving proteins, or lineage-specific innovations. Their low core genome rate (49.5%) suggests many are not conserved even within their own species. Hutchison et al. (2016) similarly found that 149 of 473 genes (31%) in their minimal *Mycoplasma* genome had unknown function -- our analysis shows this "dark matter" of essential genes is even larger when considering diverse bacteria.
heading: Orphan Essentials: The Frontier of Unknown Biology

text: Ortholog-module transfer uses fitness-module context from non-essential orthologs to infer functions for essential genes that lack direct fitness data.
quote: The ortholog-module transfer approach generated 1,382 function predictions for hypothetical essential genes. The method works because essential genes are invisible to ICA (no fitness data), but their non-essential orthologs in other organisms DO have fitness data and can participate in modules. By transferring the module's functional context across organisms, we bridge the gap between essentiality (which prevents fitness measurement) and function prediction (which requires fitness data).
heading: Module Transfer Illuminates Essential Gene Function

text: The report cites context-dependent essentiality across 36 Streptococcus pneumoniae strains and names Methanococcus and Pseudomonas as contrasting cross-species examples.
quote: - **Rosconi et al. (2022)** demonstrated context-dependent essentiality across 36 *S. pneumoniae* strains. Our work extends this concept from within-species to cross-species variation: the same gene can be essential in *Methanococcus* but dispensable in *Pseudomonas*, depending on metabolic context.
heading: Literature Context

text: The report identifies RB-TnSeq as the experimental essentiality method used across 48 organisms and contrasts it with a computational study of 52 conserved essential proteins across 14 bacterial genomes.
quote: - **Duffield et al. (2010)** identified 52 conserved essential proteins across 14 bacterial genomes as drug targets. Our approach is complementary but uses experimental (RB-TnSeq) essentiality data across 48 organisms rather than computational prediction, providing empirical validation of conservation patterns.
heading: Literature Context

text: Fitness Browser is the source fitness dataset, attributed by the report to Price et al. (2018).
quote: - **Price et al. (2018)** generated the Fitness Browser data used here. Our work adds a cross-organism essentiality dimension to their fitness data, enabling function prediction for essential genes that are outside the reach of fitness profiling.
heading: Literature Context

text: Essential-gene calls are an upper bound because lack of insertions can reflect small size, AT-rich sequence, or scaffold-edge effects rather than lethality.
quote: - **Essential gene definition is an upper bound**: Genes without transposon insertions may lack insertions due to small size, AT-rich sequence, or scaffold edge effects, not true essentiality.
heading: Limitations

text: Bidirectional-best-hit orthology can miss paralogs, gene fusions, and distant homologs, so some apparent orphan essentials may have undetected orthologs.
quote: - **BBH orthology is conservative**: Bidirectional best BLAST hits miss paralogs, gene fusions, and distant homologs. Some "orphan essentials" may have undetected orthologs with diverged sequences.
heading: Limitations

text: Connected-component grouping of the bidirectional-best-hit graph may merge unrelated genes, especially multidomain proteins.
quote: - **Connected components can over-merge**: Transitive connections in the BBH graph can merge unrelated genes into the same ortholog group, particularly for multi-domain proteins.
heading: Limitations

text: RB-TnSeq essentiality calls depend on library-construction conditions, typically rich media, and miss genes essential only under stress.
quote: - **Essentiality is condition-dependent**: RB-TnSeq essentiality is defined under specific library construction conditions (typically rich media). Genes essential only under stress would be missed.
heading: Limitations

text: The 48-organism panel is biased toward culturable Proteobacteria and underrepresents uncultured lineages, Actinobacteria, and Firmicutes.
quote: - **48 organisms is taxonomically limited**: The Fitness Browser organisms are biased toward culturable Proteobacteria. Essentiality patterns in uncultured lineages, Actinobacteria, or Firmicutes are underrepresented.
heading: Limitations

text: Module-transfer function predictions are indirect and may be wrong when an essential gene’s function has diverged from its non-essential orthologs.
quote: - **Module transfer predictions are indirect**: Function predictions for essential genes come from non-essential orthologs in other organisms. The essential gene's function may have diverged.
heading: Limitations
